facts.content: Patient was recently stung by a bee or wasp.

facts.content: Breathing appears normal on examination.

facts.source_text:
Assessment:
1. Localized allergic reaction to insect sting

facts.content: Rash and slight swelling occurred after the sting with mild but not acutely severe difficulty in breathing.
facts.source_text: Rash and slight swelling post-sting; mild difficulty in breathing, but not acutely severe

facts.content: Plan is to administer antihistamines such as pyritone or chlorphenamine 4 mg up to six times per day.
facts.source_text: Administer antihistamines such as pyritone or chlorphenamine (4 mg) up to 6 times/day

facts.content: Plan includes monitoring for spreading redness or signs of localized infection.
facts.source_text: Monitor for spreading redness or signs of localized infection

facts.content: Plan includes educating the patient on signs of allergic reactions requiring urgent care, such as severe swelling or stridor.
facts.source_text: Educate on signs of allergic reactions requiring urgent care (e.g., severe swelling, stridor)

facts.content: Plan includes providing information on anaphylactic reactions.
Patient is advised to seek follow-up if symptoms change or if recurrent reactions occur.
facts.source_text: Advise follow-up if symptoms change or if recurrent reactions occur
